claims.text: High-temperature oxidation resistance is predominantly governed by preferential oxidation of reactive elements such as Ti, Al, or Cr.
The preferentially oxidized reactive elements form a self-healing, dense spinel oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer kinetically inhibits oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 is a high-entropy alloy that has been studied at elevated temperatures including 800 and 900 °C.
The oxygen-affine elements are homogeneously distributed in the proposed alloy.
The proposed alloy has a multiphase microstructure.
Oxidizing exposure at 800–900 °C will produce a dense, coherent, spinel-type surface oxide.
A spinel oxide analogous to the MgAl2O4 structure has been observed in analogous tests.
At high temperatures, elements with high oxygen affinity oxidize preferentially.
Preferential oxidation rapidly forms a continuous and adherent spinel film.
The oxide film self-seals emerging defects through localized oxygen diffusion and reactive-element redeposition.
Self-sealing of the oxide scale limits further oxidation of the alloy interior.
An adequate reactive-element concentration will consistently produce a uniform protective oxide layer.
Reactive-element enrichment will reduce oxidation weight gain or oxidation depth relative to a composition depleted in that element.
Reactive-element enrichment will provide superior oxidation resistance relative to samples tested under inert atmospheres.
The proposed behavior applies above approximately 800 °C under oxidizing atmospheric conditions.
The protective mechanism diminishes at lower temperatures or in non-oxidizing environments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts reduced oxidation weight gain or superior oxidation resistance relative to an inert-atmosphere sample, while the inert sample is also defined as a condition in which oxidative exposure and oxide-layer formation do not occur. An inert control should ordinarily have little oxidation-related weight gain, so the stated directional comparison is internally inconsistent with its role as the no-oxidation control.
